receipt.public_excerpt: The largest size class (250+ employees) exhibits the highest use rate, rising from 5.2% to 7.8% over time

evidence_items.explanation: Even among the largest firms, under 8% reported using AI to produce goods or services by August 2024. That supports 'little evidence of significant adoption' at the firm level.

receipt.public_excerpt: Among employed respondents, 28 percent reported using generative AI for their job, with 24.2 percent using it at least one day in the previous week

evidence_items.explanation: A nationally representative survey, public before the post, found over a quarter of US workers using generative AI for their jobs. That is evidence of significant worker-level use.

unresolved_gaps: The two best measures disagree: firm-level official data show low use (under 8%), while worker surveys show over a quarter of workers using generative AI at work.
No public data isolate usage of AI features in enterprise-purchased software, the speaker's apparent focus.
The causal explanation (LLMs do not yield meaningful business returns) is hedged and was not tested with business-return data from the period.
